sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: no-passing distances, roundabout yielding, diverging diamonds, accessible parking, backing and hill parking
Look-alike rules from the passing, roundabout and parking pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Street crossings, railroad crossings and view-blocking bridges, tunnels or underpasses all share one no-passing distance of 100 feet. [A01]
Why it matters: group no passing; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F04 versus sec07-F05.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
A solid line on your side forbids passing, and a curve or hilltop that hides the road ahead forbids it too; the manual lists them as separate conditions. [A01]
Why it matters: group no passing; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F02 versus sec07-F03.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
Entering a roundabout you yield to circulating traffic and to large vehicles arriving with you, and pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the road are always yielded to as well. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F09 versus sec07-F07.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
The roundabout design speed of 15 to 20 mph is an approach speed, and once inside you keep moving rather than stopping. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty two; confusable sec07-F11 versus sec07-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A01
An emergency vehicle in a roundabout calls for proceeding with caution and exiting if you can, and only otherwise pulling over to the right. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty three; prereq sec07-F16.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A02
The diverging diamond is the design in which cross-street traffic briefly drives on the left side of the road, yet drivers get through it simply by following its signals, signs and markings. [A02]
Why it matters: group interchanges; difficulty three; confusable sec07-F20 versus sec07-F21.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A02
In a diverging diamond, traffic switches sides at the signals, and the left turns onto the on-ramps then flow freely without their own green light. [A02]
Why it matters: group interchanges; difficulty three; confusable sec07-F22 versus sec07-F24.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A03
An accessible space needs both a valid placard or plate and the person it was issued to on board; the placard alone is not enough. [A03]
Why it matters: group accessible parking; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F27.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A03
Downhill with a curb the wheels turn toward the curb, uphill with a curb they turn to the left, and with no curb they turn to the right. [A03]
Why it matters: group hill parking; difficulty three; confusable sec07-F39 versus sec07-F40.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A03
In parallel parking you turn the wheel sharply right first while backing, then sharply left once your front bumper clears the forward car. [A03]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty three; confusable sec07-F36 versus sec07-F37.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
The gap to leave beside the forward car before backing into a parallel space is about two feet, measured side to side. [A03]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty two; prereq sec07-F35.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A03
Backing safely means checking behind the car before getting in and then turning to look through the rear window, not relying on a camera or mirrors. [A03]
Why it matters: group backing; difficulty one; confusable sec07-F30 versus sec07-F31.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0030]
